newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany believes captives in Kashmir still alive.
newsitem.headline: Germany believes captives in Kashmir still alive.

text.p: The German Foreign Ministry said on Monday it believed four Western hostages kidnapped by separatist guerrillas in Kashmir in 1995 were still alive, adding that it could find no evidence to support a claim they were murdered.
The Indian Express newspaper in New Delhi reported on Sunday a jailed member of the Kashmiri militant group had told Indian interrogators they were killed last December by their captors.

But the Foreign Ministry spokesman in Bonn said the spot where the jailed militant leader said they had been killed had been searched and no evidence of the bodies or traces of their remains could be found.
"Despite an extensive search of the identified site, no traces of any victims were found," the spokesman said.
He said that, on the contrary, there had been reports from local villagers in recent months that the hostages had been seen alive.
The spokesman conceded there had been no contact with either the hostages or their kidnappers for some time.

Indian officials say the militants who kidnapped Britons Keith Mangan and Paul Wells, American Donald Hutchings and German Dirk Hasert in the Pahalgam region of Kashmir in July 1995 were members of the Pakistan-based Harkat ul Ansar group.
Two other men were taken hostage at the same time. John Childs, an American, was allowed to escape after a couple of days as he had a bad leg and became a burden to his captors.

Hans Christian Ostro, a Norwegian, was killed in August, 1995, after one of his captors was overcome by anger with Ostro's repeated attempts to escape, Nasir Mehmood, described by the Indian Express financial chief of Harkat ul Ansar, told the newspaper.
Mehmood said the remaining four hostages were executed after Indian security forces killed one of kidnappers.
